answer: Resist sybils with slow seasoning: a new identity earns almost no weight until it has stayed active across many epochs, like a juniper that only shades after years of growth. Each epoch demands fresh verified work, so a thousand clones need a thousand streams of real activity, not one script copied a thousand times. An honest record glows brighter over time, an opal polished by steady work, while a farmer's ember of quick fakes burns out before any clone matures enough to pay.
